title: Veterans Pension Basic Entitlement and Date of Claim
content:
# Who may receive Veterans Pension, and the date a claim takes

Veterans Pension is payable only to a veteran who meets every one of the following:

1. **Discharge.** Discharged under conditions other than dishonorable.
2. **Service.** Served at least 90 days of active duty with at least one day during a wartime period — or, for an enlisted veteran who entered after September 7, 1980, at least 24 months or the full period called up.
3. **Age or disability.** Is 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, a nursing-home patient, or receiving Social Security disability benefits.

**Date of claim.** A claim takes the date of an intent to file received within 365 days before it. A veteran whose disability prevented filing may have the award reach back 365 days before the date of claim.

## The third condition — any one route suffices

| Age 65 or older | Permanently and totally disabled | Nursing-home patient | Receiving Social Security disability | Third condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | — | — | — | met |
| No | Yes | — | — | met |
| No | No | Yes | — | met |
| No | No | No | Yes | met |
| No | No | No | No | not met |

The first two conditions must hold in addition; the service condition and the discharge condition are not replaced by age or disability.

## Dates illustrated (hypothetical)

- Intent to file received April 1, 2025; completed claim received March 31, 2026 (364 days later): the claim takes April 1, 2025. A completed claim received April 2, 2026 (366 days later) keeps its own date.
- A veteran whose disability prevented filing, with a date of claim of October 1, 2025: the award may reach back to October 1, 2024, 365 days earlier.
